text: Note AAU's own reminder that A, B and C are course levels, not grades; the minimum grade of 4.0 attached to Mathematics A is a grade on the Danish 7-point scale.

The standard Danish business economics degree — financing, economics, marketing, strategy and organisation — taught in English in Aalborg, with each semester built around a project done with or about a real company. It is the only one of AAU's English-taught bachelor's degrees that is not an engineering degree, and the only one based in Aalborg.

All four English-taught bachelor's degrees have restricted admission. Quota 1 ranks applicants with convertible qualifications purely on the converted grade point average. Quota 2 holds 20 per cent of places and is decided on an overall assessment: the grades in the subjects that form the entry requirements, plus documented relevant activity of up to 12 months such as work experience or supplementary education. Applicants whose grades cannot be converted to the Danish scale are assessed only in quota 2. AAU publishes the previous year's quota figure on each programme page, and 'All Admitted' means everyone qualified was offered a place that year.

The Professional Bachelor's Degree in Education (Vordingborg) is not listed: its own page says it "is taught partly in English and partly in Danish", and students who do not already meet the Danish requirement must learn Danish during the degree.
Absalon lists the biotechnology diplomingeniør as a professionsbachelor, taught in Danish or English in Kalundborg, with a study start of 1 September.

Aarhus is Denmark's second university and second city, with roughly 38,000 students and a park campus of yellow-brick buildings that runs right into the middle of town. Almost everything it teaches at bachelor level is in Danish; six degrees are taught in English, four of them in Aarhus itself, one in the small town of Herning an hour west, and all of them in computing, economics or cognitive science. AU is also unusually explicit about the numbers: every programme page publishes last year's quota 1 cut-off, the standby cut-off and the admission area number.

AU requires an IB Diploma with a minimum of 24 points. Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results or an IB Certificate of at least 18 points with grade 3 or above in every subject qualify only in combination with supplementary courses (at least two subjects, at least one at A level and one at B level, taught in Danish at VUC/GSK) or a later full IB Diploma.

The application deadline is 15 March at 12.00 noon for IB holders "regardless of whether you apply for admission in quota 1 or 2 or if you earn your IB diploma in the year of application". This is earlier than the 5 July deadline that applies to Danish-exam holders.
A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. AU repeats this on each programme page: "B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade."

AU attaches a converted-GPA floor to quota 1 on five of the six English-taught programmes: you need at least 6.0 on the Danish 7-point scale in your qualifying examination to be assessed in quota 1 at all. Below that, your application can only go through quota 2. Economics and Business Administration in Herning does not state such a floor.

Specific admission requirements: You must fulfil the following specific admission requirements: English B. Mathematics B. History B or History of Ideas B or Social Studies B or Contemporary History B. B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade. Grade point Average (GPA) requirement of 6.0 in quota 1: You must have a minimum GPA of 6.0 on the Danish 7-point grading scale in your qualifying examination to be assessed in quota 1.

Specific admission requirements: You must fulfil the following specific admission requirements: English B. Mathematics A. B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade. Grade point Average (GPA) requirement of 6.0 in quota 1: You must have a minimum GPA of 6.0 and a minimum GPA of 6.0 in Mathematics A on the Danish 7-point grading scale in your qualifying examination to be assessed in quota 1.

Mathematics, statistics and programming aimed squarely at getting reliable answers out of very large datasets. It sits between computer science and statistics and is the right choice if the appeal is the analysis rather than the systems engineering. AU states that the English-taught version is intended for international students and that it is academically equivalent to the Danish-taught Datavidenskab.

Specific admission requirements: You must fulfil the following specific admission requirements: English B. Mathematics B. History B or History of Ideas B or Social Studies B or Contemporary History B or International Economics B. B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade. Grade point Average (GPA) requirement of 6.0 in quota 1: You must have a minimum GPA of 6.0 on the Danish 7-point grading scale in your qualifying examination to be assessed in quota 1.

The standard Danish business economics degree taught in English: how a company's activities can be analysed and managed so they create value, and how to build strategies for growth. All teaching and all reading is in English because the programme is built around international business. It is the broadest of AU's English-taught degrees and the usual route into AU's business master's programmes.

A qualifying examination as well as the following specific admission requirements (A, B and C refers to the subject level in the Danish upper secondary school with A being the highest level possible): English B. Mathematics B. History B or History of Ideas B or Contemporary History B or Social Science B or International Economics B. The admission requirements must be met and documented by 5 July in the year of application unless you apply for conditional admission.

English at the Danish C-level. [...] And Mathematics at the Danish C-level. [...] Or Economics at the Danish C-level. [...] The language requirement is English at the Danish B-level (at least 210 hours during the last three years of their upper-secondary education). However, if you only fulfil the specific entry requirement of English at C level, then the language requirement can be satisfied with an English test.

CBS is a single-subject university: everything it teaches is business, economics or something deliberately bolted onto business — sociology, politics, philosophy, shipping. It has about 21,000 students on one compact campus in Frederiksberg, a tram ride from central Copenhagen, and roughly one student in five is international. Six of its fifteen bachelor programmes are taught in English and they are among the hardest degrees in Denmark to get into on grades alone: in 2026 the quota 1 cut-off for International Business was 11.1 out of a maximum 12.

CBS's deadline table gives 15 March 12.00 CET for both quota 1 and quota 2 if your exam is international. This is earlier than the 5 July quota 1 deadline that applies to holders of a Danish upper secondary exam. The portal optagelse.dk opens on 1 February.

CBS accepts the IB Diploma as equivalent to a Danish upper secondary exam only if it has at least 24 points including bonus and minus penalty points, at least 6 subjects, at least 3 and no more than 4 subjects at Higher Level, a submitted Extended Essay, a completed Theory of Knowledge course and all CAS activities completed.
The IB Diploma is a convertible exam at CBS, so you are assessed in both quota 1 and quota 2. Your total points are converted to the Danish scale using the Ministry's conversion table.

Grade conversion for single subjects is blunt and worth memorising: CBS states "Danish grade 2.0 = local grade 3" and "Danish grade 6.0 = local grade 5". Every English-taught programme requires English B with a minimum grade of 6.0, so in practice you need at least a 5 in your IB English subject.

A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. The minimum grade of 6.0 attached to English B (and to Mathematics B on the Sociology programme) is a grade on the Danish 7-point scale, and corresponds to an IB subject grade of 5 under CBS's own conversion.
CBS does not round up: "If you have passed a subject with an average grade of 5.5 on the Danish scale and the grade requirement is 6.0, you do not meet the requirement. We do not round grades up."

Mathematics B must be passed with a minimum grade of 6.0 on the Danish scale, which is an IB grade of 5. IB Mathematics at HL satisfies this automatically, because a subject passed at A level fulfils any B-level grade requirement.
The Danish page says students on Cyber Security can finish after two years or continue to the full professionsbachelor. Either way, you apply to the professionsbachelor programme.

Specific entry requirements: English at the Danish B-level. This means that international applicants must have had English for at least 210 hours (60 minutes each) during the last three years of their upper-secondary education. And Mathematics at the Danish B-level. This means that international applicants must have had mathematics for at least 250 hours (60 minutes each) during the last three years of their upper-secondary education.

DTU is Denmark's main technical university, on a large purpose-built campus in Kongens Lyngby about 15 km north of central Copenhagen. Almost all of its teaching is engineering and natural science, and its undergraduate degrees are mostly taught in Danish. For an IB student the practical point is that DTU has exactly one full English-taught bachelor's degree, General Engineering, where roughly 60 per cent of the students come from outside Denmark.
Quota 1 deadline (Danish qualifying exam only) and final grades
Only for applicants with a Danish qualifying exam; also the deadline for submitting final grades and diploma.

DTU states: "DTU currently offers one English-taught full degree BSc programme in General Engineering. All other undergraduate programmes are taught in Danish, but we offer a wide range of individual courses in English."

Quota 1 is a pure GPA ranking and is open to IB holders as well as to Danish, Nordic and EU/EEA school leavers. Quota 2 is for applicants with a school-leaving exam from outside the EU/EEA, or for anyone who thinks their GPA is too low for quota 1; EU/EEA and IB applicants who apply in quota 2 are automatically also assessed in quota 1. DTU says the quota 1 cut-off "is the GPA of the last applicant admitted through Quota 1, and it is not known until the admission process is completed on July 28th", so no cut-off is published in advance.
ITU converts IB grades to the Danish 7-point scale; it gives IB grade 3 = Danish 2 and IB grade 5 = Danish 7 as worked examples.

Read the Danish requirement carefully: BSc Global Business Informatics is taught in English but still demands Danish at A level as a passed subject, so in practice it is open only to applicants who have studied Danish. ITU's own BSc overview page says "only the programme in Data Science is open to international students".

From the 2027 admission round ITU requires an overall GPA of at least 6.0 on the Danish 7-point scale for BSc Software Development. Check whether a similar floor has been added to the English-taught degrees before applying.
Danish
71 study places in 2026; 92 per cent of those admitted had Danish qualifications.

A degree about how organisations actually use digital technology — AI, business analytics and digital transformation — rather than about building the technology itself. It is taught in English, but be warned: you must also have passed Danish at A level, so it is realistically only open to applicants who went to school in Denmark or studied Danish to A level.

The Royal Danish Academy is Denmark's national school of architecture, design and conservation, based in Copenhagen. Its one English-taught first degree is not in Copenhagen: Crafts in Glass and Ceramics is taught in the glass and ceramics workshops in Nexø on Bornholm, a Baltic island reached from Copenhagen by train and ferry. The whole intake is decided by admission tests, not grades.
Royal Danish Academy – Architecture, Design, Conservation

A number of internationally recognized exams of the type "Baccalaureat" (like IB and EB) are considered equivalent to a Danish "stx" (3-year high school), and we have no further requirements regarding contents and level of subjects apart from English at level B. [...] IB English B (SL).
Royal Danish Academy
An IB counts as equivalent to a Danish stx. Apart from English B, there are no subject, level or grade-average requirements.
Applicants need English at Danish B level. An IB meets it with English B at SL or higher; otherwise TOEFL, IELTS Academic 6.5 or Cambridge C1/C2 at 180. No dispensation is possible.

Roskilde University was set up in 1972 to experiment with how knowledge is taught, and it still works differently from every other Danish university. You do not apply to a named subject. You apply to one of three broad international bachelor programmes, spend the whole first year in an interdisciplinary basic studies section, and only then choose the two bachelor subjects you will study for the remaining two years. Roughly half of all study time is group project work on real problems rather than lectures and exams, and the campus at Trekroner, 30 minutes by train from Copenhagen, has about 7,900 students.
optagelse.dk is open from 1 February to 15 March, 12 noon CET. This deadline covers IB, European Baccalaureate, Danish/French Baccalaureate and exemption-based applications.

RUC lists the International Baccalaureate among the international qualifications that satisfy its general admission requirement, but its English pages do not publish a minimum IB point score or a subject-by-subject IB-to-Danish conversion table.
If your qualification is not on RUC's list, you can ask RUC for a pre-assessment or have it assessed by the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science.
Guaranteed admission in 2026 for applicants who met all requirements and had a Danish-converted GPA of at least 2.0.
A minimum grade requirement applies: either an overall GPA of 6.0 on the Danish 7-point scale, or an average of 4.0 across English and Mathematics.
Guaranteed admission in 2026 for applicants who met all requirements and had a Danish-converted GPA of at least 9.0.

English at Danish B-level. Mathematics at Danish B-level. History or Social Science or Contemporary History or History of Ideas at Danish B-level. You must also meet one of the following minimum grade requirements: a grade point average of at least 6.0 on the Danish 7-point grading scale from your entry qualification, or an average of at least 4.0 on the Danish 7-point grading scale in English and Mathematics combined.
Guaranteed admission in 2026 for applicants who met all requirements and had a Danish-converted GPA of at least 8.5.

RUC runs a guaranteed-admission scheme rather than relying only on a published cut-off: "if you meet all admission requirements and you have the equivalent of the required Danish GPA, you are guaranteed admission." For the 2026 intake the guaranteed-admission GPAs were 2.0 for International Bachelor in Natural Sciences, 8.5 for Global Humanities and 9.0 for International Bachelor in Social Sciences. Guaranteed admission is not available to applicants holding qualifications from outside the EU/EEA, because "your grades cannot be converted directly to the Danish grading scale"; those applicants are assessed in quota 2.

SDU is spread across seven towns in the south and west of Denmark, and where you study matters more here than at any other Danish university. Its headquarters and most of its Danish-taught teaching are in Odense, but almost every fully English-taught bachelor's degree sits in Sønderborg, a small town on the island of Als by the German border, or in Vejle, SDU's newest campus and an IT-focused one. SDU is also unusual in how it admits people: an aptitude test called uniTEST is used for quota 2 on nearly all programmes, and SDU openly recommends that everyone sit it, including applicants whose grades would be good enough for quota 1.
SDU has already published the 2027 dates: 17 and 18 April 2027, written and paper-based, at Campusvej 55, 5230 Odense M. If you are in Denmark on the test date you must attend in person.
20–25 April 2027, taken online on your own computer with a live supervisor, if you are not in Denmark on the test dates. Your computer and room must meet technical requirements.

SDU also has campuses in Kolding, Esbjerg, Slagelse and Copenhagen. None of them currently offers a fully English-taught bachelor's degree, so they are not options for an IB student who does not read Danish.

Robot Systems (Robotteknologi) in Odense is often assumed to be English-taught. It is not: SDU lists its tuition language as Danish. Robotics in English at SDU means Mechatronics in Sønderborg at bachelor level.

International Business Administration, Language and Culture (Sønderborg and EUF Flensborg) is listed among SDU's international programmes but is excluded here: SDU gives its tuition language as "English, German and Danish" and it requires Danish level A plus German at A or B level. It took only 6 students in 2026.
A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. SDU repeats this on every programme page: "A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level."
Quota 1 GPA floor: "To be considered for a study place in quota 1, your GPA must be equivalent to 7.0 or higher in the Danish grading scale."
In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale.
Quota 1 GPA floor of 5.0 on the Danish scale.
Quota 1 GPA floor: from 2027 your GPA must be equivalent to 7.0 or higher on the Danish scale to be considered in quota 1 (it was 6.0 until 2026).
SDU prints the third requirement as "International Economy level B"; this is the Danish subject International Economics (International Økonomi).

A broad business economics degree with everything framed around companies that trade across borders — fitting, given that the campus sits on the German border. Your year group will be Danish and other European students, taught entirely in English. It has the lowest quota 1 grade floor of SDU's non-engineering English-taught degrees.

An interdisciplinary social science degree about how European regions, institutions and cross-border co-operation actually work, taught in small classes on the Danish-German border — which is the live case study. You learn to design and run development projects with a regional, national or European focus and to explain the results to decision-makers.
Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale — this still applies even in a year when everyone qualified was admitted.

In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Physics level B or Geoscience level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
Quota 1 GPA floor: "To be considered for a study place in quota 1, your GPA must be equivalent to 5.0 or higher in the Danish grading scale."

SDU runs the usual Danish quota 1 and quota 2 split, but quota 2 at SDU is almost entirely an aptitude test called uniTEST. Quota 1 is decided on converted grade point average, and unusually SDU also sets a published minimum GPA to be considered in quota 1 at all: 7.0 on most BSc programmes, 6.0 on Economics and Business Administration in Sønderborg, and 5.0 on the three Bachelor of Engineering (BEng) programmes. Fall below it and your application can only be assessed in quota 2. Quota 2 places go to the applicants with the highest uniTEST scores. SDU says in its own words: "We recommend that everyone apply through quota 2 at SDU, even those with a grade point average sufficient to apply through quota 1." EU/EEA applicants whose grades convert are assessed on GPA unless they also sit the test; all non-EU/EEA applicants are invited to uniTEST because their grades are not converted. uniTEST is not a subject exam — it tests critical, quantitative and linguistic thinking, and all the information needed is given in the test.

The single most important fact about the University of Copenhagen, for anyone finishing an IB, is that you cannot study there at bachelor level without fluent academic Danish. UCPH says it plainly on its own bachelor page: "UCPH only offers bachelor's degree programmes taught in Danish." All 78 bachelor's degrees are in Danish; the English-taught offering begins at master's level. It is Denmark's oldest and largest university, founded in 1479, with about 36,800 students across six faculties and four campuses in and around central Copenhagen — and if you want it, you need to plan a Danish-language route into it years in advance, not in your final IB year.
Applying in quota 2 commits you to the quota 2 test and an interview held in Danish, Norwegian or Swedish.

There is a hard grade floor: "In addition to having accomplished an IB Diploma, you must present a grade point average equivalent to the Danish 6.0 – or more." Below a converted 6.0 you cannot be considered in quota 1.

Danish language is a requirement for every bachelor's degree. If your A HL/SL or B HL Language or Literature subject is not Danish, Norwegian or Swedish, you must pass Studieprøven i dansk som andetsprog or document equivalent academic Danish. Danish B at HL normally exempts you.
Students from the Nordic countries with Danish, Norwegian or Swedish in their upper secondary education do not have to sit a Danish language test.

Subject conversion follows the Danish Agency's handbook: IB Mathematics HL/SL counts as Matematik A/B, Physics HL/SL as Fysik A/B, English A1/A2 at SL or HL as Engelsk A, and Danish A1 HL as the Danish requirement.

There are no fully English-taught bachelor's degrees at the University of Copenhagen. UCPH's own bachelor page reads: "Kickstart your career at UCPH and explore 78 bachelor's degree programmes - all are taught in Danish" and, separately, "UCPH only offers bachelor's degree programmes taught in Danish." The programmes list below is therefore empty, and that is the accurate answer rather than an omission.
Quota 2 at UCPH involves a test and an interview conducted in Danish, Norwegian or Swedish — a further reason why applying without the language is not viable.
A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. The 6.0 is a grade point average on the Danish 7-point scale.

Quota 1 is a ranking on the converted grade point average from your first given exam certificate, and you need at least a converted 6.0 to be in it at all. Quota 2 at UCPH is not a paper exercise: applicants must sit and pass a quota 2 test and take part in an interview, and UCPH states that "Applicants who have not participated and passed the quota 2-test will not be considered for admission" in that quota. The interview is held in Danish, Norwegian or Swedish, which is a further reason the Danish requirement is not a formality. Quota 2 selection is an overall assessment of the test and the interview. The quota 2 application deadline is 15 March at 12:00; quota 1 applicants have until 5 July at 12:00. Offers are published on 28 July.

The English-proficiency rule is shared across VIA: English at Danish B level with a weighted average of at least 2.0, or an accepted test such as IELTS Academic 6.5. A test cannot replace English where a programme names it as a specific requirement.
VIA teaches in Danish on its other campuses (Aarhus among them). Only the three campuses with an English-taught first degree are listed here.

Admission requirements - One of the following: Upper secondary school leaving certificate/high school exam; The International or the European Baccalaureate; The Danish Admission course for Engineering programmes; [...] Specific admission requirements: A C-level in Mathematics = 125 instructional hours of 60 minutes each. [...] Each of the subjects above must be passed with a min. average of 2.0 on the Danish grading scale.

The International or the European Baccalaureate with Mathematics equivalent to a Danish C-level [...] A Mathematics C-level is 125 instructional hours of 60 minutes each. [...] Each of the subjects above must be passed with a min. average of 2.0 on the Danish grading scale.

Mathematics equivalent to a Danish C-level (125 instructional hours of 60 minutes each). English equivalent to a Danish B-level (210 hours instructional hours of 60 minutes each) or a Danish C-level (75 hours instructional hours of 60 minutes each) AND a valid English test. All of the above subjects must be passed with a minimum average of 2.0 on the Danish grading scale.

You can apply based on a foreign upper secondary school certificate (high school, baccalaureate, IB or similar). [...] All applicants (including native English speakers) must document English proficiency. It must be equivalent to a Danish B-level with a minimum weighted grade point average score of 2.0 on the Danish grading scale.

Every VIA English-taught programme needs English at Danish B level with a weighted average of at least 2.0, or an accepted test (IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 94 before 21 January 2026 or 4.5 after, Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency at 180). A test cannot replace English where it is a specific entry requirement.
Non-EU applicants without a Danish residence permit that gives free tuition pay a one-time application fee of EUR 300 by 15 March. It is deducted from the first year's tuition if they accept a place.

The International Baccalaureate + Mathematical Studies, standard level (SL). [...] English B or equivalent level of English. A Danish B-level in English is a minimum of 210 study hours of 60 minutes each obtained during the final three years in Upper Secondary School. You may also fulfill the English requirements with one of the following test results [...]

The International Baccalaureate + Mathematical Studies, standard level (SL). [...] Please note that the English requirements cannot be replaced by an English test, as English B is a specific requirement for admission to the program, whether it is the Danish- or English-taught version.

IB results are released on 6 July. Danish applications close on 15 March, so you apply before you have your results and ask your IB coordinator to send them directly through the IB's results service (up to six institutions).

Check the letter at the bottom left of your diploma. D is an original result, R is a retake. If you retook to improve a result that already qualified you, Denmark converts your ORIGINAL result, not the improved one.
This is a genuine and useful difference from what several Danish university pages say. The agency's handbook is the governing source.

The supplement must consist of two successive raises of subject level, at least one of them to A-level. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B-level are enough. Supplementary subjects are taken as hf-enkeltfag, or as a self-study candidate, and are taught in Danish.
Nothing — not a qualifying examination in Denmark
An IB Diploma with 24 points or more gives access to every higher education programme in Denmark, provided you also meet the programme's specific subject requirements.

Every Danish institution converts IB results using this handbook. Individual university pages are often out of date; this is the source they are all supposed to follow.
Danish B HL or Danish ab initio — decided institution by institution. Ask in writing.

Prepared by the Danish Ministry of Children and Education. Danish levels are A (highest), B and C — they are levels of study, not grades.

Global Politics is 150 hours at SL and 240 at HL. Danish Social Studies (samfundsfag) B covers sociology, economics, politics and method; A adds international politics. Global Politics goes far deeper into international politics than Danish Social Studies A, but does not cover the sociology and economics that the Danish subject includes. Institutions decide case by case whether it meets Social Studies C, B or A — sometimes only in combination with another social science subject.

TOK does not correspond to any subject in the Danish upper secondary system. Depending on what you covered, it may earn credit towards small parts of certain Danish subjects, but it does not satisfy a subject requirement.

It does not close this one to you. The Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three of them at HL, as equivalent to a qualifying examination for a Danish university bachelor once you have added two successive raises in the level of upper-secondary subjects, at least one of them to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag or as a self-study candidate. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B level are enough. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the other published route.

The rule is national rather than this university's: the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science sets which examinations are adgangsgivende, and every Danish institution applies the same one. Two things about it are easy to get wrong. GSK (gymnasial supplering) cannot be used for this — GSK raises a subject level for someone who already holds a qualifying examination, so it meets a specific subject requirement but never raises the level of the examination itself. And the average used in quota 1 is the one from the first qualifying examination, so a Course Results holder who supplements or retakes is still converted on the original Course Results result.

The rule is national, not this institution's. The Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with grade 3 or more in all six subjects and three at HL, like a two-year hf without overbygning, which gives access to erhvervsakademi and professionsbachelor programmes through quota 1 and quota 2. This is a diplomingeniør programme at a university college, which is a professionsbachelor programme: Absalon lists the programme on its Danish page as a professionsbachelor ("Professionsbachelor — Diplomingeniør i bioteknologi"). The institution's own page names the IB but says nothing about Course Results, so a Course candidate should confirm with admissions in writing. The award does not waive the subject requirements below.

A qualifying examination certificate that can be equated with a Danish upper secondary school leaving certificate. Mathematics corresponding to the Danish B-level with an average mark of at least 6. English corresponding to the Danish B-level with an average mark of at least 6. Danish at A level is a requirement. No required mark but the subject must be passed. You must be proficient in oral and written English, as the programme is taught in English.

Roskilde states this as an either/or: a beginner’s language needs A level (325 hours of instruction), an advanced language needs B level (200 hours). SDU publishes two different IB rules on one page, and the difference between them is the whole point. For a bachelor's programme it asks a Course candidate to have "supplemented with at least two individual subjects (minimum one at A-level subject and one at B-level subject)". For a Bachelor of Engineering it asks for nothing beyond the six subjects at grade 3 with three at HL. So a Course candidate reaches this programme with the award as it stands, and no hf-enkeltfag are needed. The national order underneath that: the Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points as equal to a two-year hf without overbygning, and an hf without overbygning is adgangsgivende to a diplomingeniør-uddannelse but not to a universitetsbacheloruddannelse. SDU's own Danish list of qualifying examinations says exactly that — "Eksamener, der kun giver adgang til diplomingeniøruddannelser: Højere forberedelseseksamen (hf) uden overbygning aflagt efter gymnasiereformen 2017" — and DTU publishes the same restriction for its own diplomingeniør intake. Two things this does not do. It does not waive the subject requirements below: Mathematics A, English B and Physics B or Geoscience A still bind, and a Course candidate meets them with IB subjects on the same conversion as anybody else. And the 18-point floor recorded here is the Agency's rather than SDU's: below 18 points, or with any subject at grade 1 or 2, the Course Results are not a qualifying examination at all and no Danish programme is reachable. Grade 3 in all six subjects already puts the subject total at 18, so the two conditions meet in the same place.
